definition: Backup power provides an alternative electricity supply that allows project-supported operations to continue when the primary power supply is unavailable. Counts when the project finances, procures, installs or explicitly requires generators, batteries, uninterruptible power supplies, redundant power feeds, stored fuel or another identifiable backup-power arrangement. The defining function is continuity during loss of the primary electricity supply, not the source of the electricity. Renewable generation used as backup may also count under renewable_energy when renewable electricity supply is itself an explicit project objective. Does not count for general electricity access, grid strengthening, power-sector investments, improved electricity reliability without a specific backup arrangement, or statements that reliable power is important.
note: Classify by function. Renewable electricity used as the normal or primary supply belongs to renewable_energy; electricity specifically available when the primary supply fails belongs here.
